correctness.rationale: The binary best-response condition is exactly adjacent edge disagreements unequal or both equal the player type. Reachability of at least 3 of 4 cumulative-XOR states proves feasibility of each fixed-endpoint C/R chain. Splitting at pins covers all nonempty pinned cycles, including coincident endpoints for a single pin. One-pin alternating cycles yield weakly decreasing transformed-bit words, and cyclic XOR closure selects the stated parity class; the fixed action ensures unique lift. Exhaustive separate direct-payoff checks through n=8 (all C/R/S0/S1), one-pin counts to n=16, and a three-action counterexample agree. Finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: One fixed-action vertex resolves the established binary alternating-cycle no-PNE obstruction for all conformist/rebel arrangements, even where generic sufficient conditions fail. The exact multiplicity n/2 on previously frustrated cycle lengths quantitatively distinguishes restoration from existence alone. The rigorous two-action versus three-action boundary is useful for the recent CRS network-game literature and is not an arbitrary finite instance.
